messages.author: 25ce5e85187da1a3
messages.subject: Approximation error of INLA?
parts:
Dear INLA experts,

How can we assess the error approximations done by INLA, and how can I obtain the approximation error of INLA from an r-inla output? Is there a simple way to do it?

Thank you very much in advance,

Burak Kursad Gunhan

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Approximation error of INLA?
parts:
On Tue, 2016-08-16 at 06:24 -0700, Burak Gunhan wrote:
> Dear INLA experts,
>
> How can we assess the error approximations done by INLA, and how can
> I obtain the approximation error of INLA from an r-inla output? Is
> there a simple way to do it?
>
> Thank you very much in advance,
>

you cannot. there is a long discussion of this in the INLA paper. 

you can study the difference of increasingly accurate approximation,
but that is not failsafe either. there is now a lot of empirical
studies, and personally, I'm not that worried anymore. 

there is also a good discussion of this issue here


http://arxiv.org/abs/1604.00860

H


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

messages.author: 25ce5e85187da1a3
messages.subject: Re: Approximation error of INLA?
parts:
Dear INLA experts,

In one of the slides of "Bayesian statistics with R-INLA (Zurich)" course, it is written that we can compare "effective number of parameters" as is defined in DIC and compare it with number of observartions. And the low ratio means good if we want to assess the error in the approximations. Then it is written that this criteria has theoretical justification.

My question is that can you refer me any paper which explains that "theoretical justification"?

Thank you

Burak
